messages.author: e169f11d9c98fa98
messages.subject: <Q> Data format by transect line in a region
parts:
Dear all

I am a beginner to Distance sampling.

Ten transect lines were set up in one area (Defalt) (L-1.... .L-10).

We want to compare seabird density, etc. by line, so the data format
was as follows. (sample_data, of course)

Region.Label, Area, Sample_Label, Effort, distance, size
Default, 10, L-1, 6, 0.1, 1
Default, 10, L-1, 6, 0.2, 10
Default, 10, L-2, 7, 0.3, 5
Default, 10, L-2, 7, 0.9, 5
Default, 10, L-3, 8, 0.3, 2
Default, 10, L-3, 8, 0.1, 2
Default, 10, L-4, 3, 0.1, 1
Default, 10, L-4, 3, 0.2, 10
Default, 10, L-4, 3, 0.3, 13
...................cont................
Default, 10, L-10, 5, 0.3, 11
Default, 10, L-10, 5, 0.2, 8

This data format could be read and calculated by Distance for Windows.
However, the R version of Distance reads the data but gives an error
in the calculation of the ds function.

model <- ds(data =sample_data ,
+ transect = "line",
+ key = "hn", # half normal
+ adjustment = "cos", # cos
+ order = 2,
+ truncation = 0.3) #

...checkdata(data, region_table, sample_table, obs_table, formula) ERROR:
...Region areas are not consistent.
...Unknown or uninitialised column: `distbegin`.

How should the data format be arranged?

When I renamed Default in Region.Label to Default+Line-no, no more
error messages.

Why is this?
Was this the solution?

Best
Yasuo SHIMADA

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: <Q> Data format by transect line in a region
parts:
Yasuo

These principles of distance sampling will help guide you in organising your data.

You define a study area about which you want to make inference of population size. Because you define the study area, you know its size. That is the value you provide in the "Area" column.

Into that study area, you randomly place transects, named in the column "Sample.Label" (not "Sample_Label" as you show in the first line of the file you provide). Those transects are of known length (specified by "Effort").

The value of "Area" should be the same for all rows with a given "Region.Label" designation; if not, the error you noted will be generated.

The value of the "Area" field is not computed in the manner  you suggest; it is defined when the study area is delineated.
